title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing — May 2028
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging proposals, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family as of May 2028. It is intended for cross-functional stakeholders (product, engineering, SRE, sales, and finance) to align on scope, success metrics, and the upcoming release and commercial plans.

Intro & context
----------------
Redwood's Unified Inference product provides a single API and operational surface across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployment modes. The 2028 strategy emphasizes predictable unit economics, multi-variant model routing, fine-grained cost controls (batching, quantization), and enterprise readiness for regulated customers. This PRD and roadmap focus on:
- Improving latency/cost tradeoffs for tail-latency sensitive customers
- Making model routing and fallbacks first-class configuration for customers
- Shipping new pricing tiers and packaging for cross-sell into Dedicated and Private
- Delivering a safe, observable rollout with backward-compatible APIs

Goals & success metrics
-----------------------
Primary goals (90-day and 12-month):
1) Reduce median per-request cost for typical chat workloads by 15% (by Sep 2028).
2) Add model-routing policies and fallback configuration with SLO-aware routing for at least 3 major enterprise customers by Q4 2028.
3) Launch pricing & packaging that increases ARPU for Dedicated installs by 20% while keeping conversion for self-serve Hosted customers flat.
4) Improve observable regressions detection: integrate prompt-set based quality monitoring into release pipeline (target: detect 95% of regressions within 24 hours).

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Per-token unit cost (USD) — target: -15% vs baseline by Sep 2028
- Latency P95/P99 for standard chat workload — target: P95 <= 220ms, P99 <= 480ms for hosted small-model profile
- Model routing adoption (customers with custom routing policies) — target: 10 paying customers by Q4 2028
- Revenue uplift from new pricing tiers — target: +20% ARR from Dedicated packaging after 6 months

PRD: Requirements (high level)
----------------------------
User stories (representative):
- As a product engineer, I want to configure a policy that routes low-latency requests to a smaller model and high-quality requests to a larger model so my application meets latency SLOs while controlling cost.
- As a platform engineer, I need predictable throughput for Dedicated customers with configurable autoscaling and burst windows.
- As a security officer, I want Private deployments to support KMS/HSM-backed keys and audit logging for model inputs/outputs.

Functional requirements:
1) Model routing & fallbacks
   - Expose routing policy API allowing predicates (latency budget, cost budget, region)
   - Fallback chains: when target variant unavailable, route to compatible variant with preserved schema
   - Policy preview: simulate routing on historical traces for cost/latency estimation
2) Cost controls and optimizer suggestions
   - Batching/quantization recommendation engine with per-route suggestions
   - Per-route token and request quotas with alerting
3) Dedicated & Private capabilities
   - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, configurable concurrency/throughput targets, SLA metrics
   - Private: VPC networking, KMS integrations, air-gapped deployment option, and permissions mirroring Hosted features
4) Observability & quality monitoring
   - Prompt-set exports, evaluation harness integrations, regression alerts (threshold and model-based)
   - Token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Console and API
5) API & compatibility
   - New routing and cost-control fields should be additive and backwards-compatible with existing text/generate/chat endpoints

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Latency: end-to-end P95 targets for small-model profiles 220ms; P99 480ms (hosted)
- Reliability: 99.95% uptime SLA for Dedicated core inference endpoints
- Scalability: support sudden request spikes (x3 baseline) with graceful degradation policies
- Security: FIPS-compliant crypto options for Private KMS integrations (when required by customer)

Design specs (high level)
-----------------------
Architecture overview:
- Control plane
  - Policy service: stores routing policies, evaluates predicates for incoming requests
  - Planner & simulator: runs preview simulations over historical traces to estimate cost/latency impact
  - Billing adaptor: aggregates per-token/per-request metadata for pricing pipelines
- Data plane (serving runtime)
  - Router: lightweight edge that enforces routing decision and selects model variant
  - Inference pool: model variant instances with automatic KV cache sharing, continuous batching, and quantized execution paths
  - Telemetry exporter: emits token-level and request-level metrics to Console and observability backend

APIs (additive fields):
- POST /v1/routing-policies -> create/update policy
- GET /v1/routing-policies/preview?trace_id= -> returns cost/latency simulation for policy
- New generate/chat request fields: routing_policy_id (optional), cost_budget_usd (optional), latency_budget_ms (optional)

Configuration table (example)
- The following table shows example policy fields (presented as key: description):
  - id: unique policy id
  - name: human-friendly name
  - predicates: list of predicate clauses (e.g., region == "eu-west-1", latency_budget_ms <= 200)
  - variants: ordered list of model variants with weights and compatibility tags
  - fallback_chain: ordered fallback variants if primary fails
  - cost_budget_usd: optional per-request budget for automatic fallback / response truncation

Data schema notes:
- Telemetry: all requests must attach request_id, route_id, policy_id (if present), model_variant_id, input_token_count, output_token_count, start_time_ms, end_time_ms
- Audit logs (Private): must include hashed user identifiers, encrypted payload references when requested

Roadmap & themes (high level quarters)
------------------------------------
Themes for H2 2028 and near-term 2029:
- Theme: Cost Predictability & Controls (Q3 2028)
  - Deliver policy preview simulator, per-route cost budgets, and first-pass optimizer suggestions
- Theme: Enterprise Routing & Reliability (Q4 2028)
  - SLO-aware routing, Dedicated autoscaling policy improvements, SLA onboarding playbook
- Theme: Packaging & Monetization (Q4 2028 — Q1 2029)
  - New Dedicated pricing tiers, Private deployment packaging, cross-sell offers with extended observability retention
- Theme: Quality Guardrails & Evals (Q1 2029)
  - Integrate prompt-set regression alerts into CI/CD and provide automated rollback hooks

Quarterly roadmap (milestones):
- May 2028 (current): PRD sign-off, API contract draft, design spike complete
- Jun–Jul 2028: Implement routing policy CRUD, basic Router integration, and telemetry schema v1
- Aug 2028: Policy preview simulator + telemetry-backed cost estimation; Console UI for routing policies (alpha)
- Sep 2028: Beta for SLO-aware routing with 3 pilot customers; optimizer suggestions v1
- Nov 2028: Dedicated packaging finalized; pricing experiments start; SLA documentation published
- Jan 2029: General availability of routing and pricing packages; quality monitoring integration with release pipeline

Pricing & packaging notes (proposals)
----------------------------------
Objectives for pricing changes:
- Align incentives so customers pay for value (latency, throughput, and quality) rather than raw premium hardware alone.
- Create entry, scale, and enterprise tiers that map to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private features.

Proposed tiers (summary):
1) Developer (Hosted, self-serve)
   - Usage-based: per-token generation and embedding pricing (no commitment)
   - Included: basic routing (single default policy), 30-day telemetry retention, free-tier credits for trial
2) Scale (Hosted + Dedicated trial)
   - Committed usage discount (monthly/annual), per-route optimizer suggestions, policy preview simulator access
   - SLA: 99.9% uptime for critical endpoints
3) Enterprise (Dedicated + Private)
   - Monthly/annual reserved capacity pricing, enterprise support, extended telemetry retention, private deployment license, KMS/HSM options
   - Add-on: Advanced observability retention, compliance evidence package, SOC2+ audit assistance

Pricing experiments & measurement:
- Run A/B tests with 5 pilot customers for Dedicated packaging (Nov 2028) to measure conversion delta and ARPU uplift.
- Track churn and expansion metrics monthly to validate packaging alignment with customer value.

Release notes (May 2028 — initial rollout)
-----------------------------------------
Release: unified-inference-routing-2028-05 (beta)
Highlights:
- API: routing policy CRUD endpoints (alpha), additive request fields (routing_policy_id, latency_budget_ms, cost_budget_usd)
- Control plane: policy evaluator and preview simulator v0.1 (batch simulation over 30-day trace)
- Data plane: Router integration for variant selection, telemetry v1 with token-level cost/latency fields
- Console: routing policy basic UI (alpha), per-route cost breakdown view

Known limitations & caveats:
- Policy preview uses sampled traces; accuracy will improve as trace coverage increases
- Fallbacks currently only support variants within same model family (schema compatibility required)
- SLO-aware routing will be available in beta in Sep 2028 (not in initial release)

Rollout & canary plan:
1) Internal dogfood (2 weeks): internal teams and known pilot apps run on feature flags
2) Pilot customers (4 customers, 4 weeks): opt-in beta for routing and simulator
3) Gradual availability: enable for 10% of eligible Hosted traffic with automatic telemetry monitoring for regressions
4) Full GA: after beta feedback, and successful pricing experiments (target Jan 2029)

Operational runbook (high-level)
------------------------------
- Monitoring: Add telemetry alert thresholds: token cost growth > 30% week-over-week, P99 latency increase > 20%
- Escalation: On detected regressions, automatic rollback of routing policy changes and notify oncall-product -> oncall-sre
- Rollback steps: disable routing_policy_id flag at edge, fail-open to default model variant, open postmortem if customer impact > 1% requests

Open decisions (to be resolved before GA)
--------------------------------------
1) Pricing unit for cost budgets: should we bill per-request budget consumption or normalize to per-token charges? (decision due 2028-08-01)
2) Fallback compatibility rules: strict same-model-family vs typed-schema compatibility (decision due 2028-07-15)
3) Minimum reserved capacity for Dedicated tier: 50% utilization guarantee or smaller entry commitment? (decision due 2028-09-01)

------------------------

- Eng: complete policy evaluator and start Router integration work (owner: Jordan, due: 2028-07-15)
- Sales/Finance: draft Dedicated pricing experiment plan and pilot customer list (owner: Priya, due: 2028-09-01)
- Security: define Private deployment KMS/HSM acceptance criteria (owner: Marcus, due: 2028-06-30)
